issues.issue: 2020 gambling loss deduction beyond the $6,653 respondent allowed
issues.court: 61929 allowed (losses at least equal to winnings)
issues.diagnosis: The decisive step is the Cohan estimate that losses were at least equal to winnings (judgment on coin-in $105,063, casino visits, few assets); given that finding, the §165(d) cap at gambling gains ($61,929) is computed and matches.
issues.snippet: Petitioner is entitled to deduct $61,929 of gambling losses for the year in issue.

issues.lean: applies (via negligence; substantial understatement false on known items)
issues.diagnosis: §6751(b) approval (2022-08-16, before assessment) and no reasonable cause are encoded as the court found them. The court did not name the ground. On the items the opinion states (conceded mortgage interest $7,200 and charity $3,050), Lean's partial understatement is $1,230 (TI 20,901 vs 10,651), not substantial (< $5,000); the rest of the underpayment (car/truck $9,315 on Schedule C with unstated profit, settled 'omitted items of income') is not in the opinion. Penalty applies in Lean only because negligence is encoded from the court's implied finding (concessions unexplained, no records); the ground and reasonable cause are judgments. Penalty amount left to Rule 155.
issues.snippet: petitioner failed to act with reasonable cause and in good faith. Therefore, petitioner is liable for an accuracy-related penalty
